description: Vectors of the contact measure behind `volumes-connected` and of the sheet judgement and the per-scale judgement of `volumes-feature`. All lengths in metres, y up, the ground is y = 0. A solid is an axis-aligned cuboid (`centre`, `size`), optionally turned by `turnZDeg` about the z axis through its centre, optionally repeated: `copies` are the centres of the copies of one solid (its `repeat`). The smallest feature is that of 1:50 (7.5 mm), so the contact tolerance is 1.5 mm (a fifth), the clearance 7.5 mm (one feature) and the gap cap 45 mm (six features). Every expected value is derived by hand in `hand`. `structures` cases may carry `en` and `de`: fragments that the finding of `volumes-connected` for the structure list of 1:50 contains, and `absent`: fragments that no message contains. `spans` holds the vectors of the member solids that span several bones (`members`).

declarations.hand: limits 7.5 mm (1:50) and 75 mm (1:500), ratio 20; `thin` counts the findings of a dimension below the limit, `hint` whether that finding asks for `sheet: true`, `declaration` the findings of a `sheet` that is no thin sheet, `both` those of `sheet` with `slender`, `ratio` the middle extent over the thickness. A plate 300 x 300 x 1 mm: 300 >= max(7.5, 20) and 300 >= max(75, 20), a sheet at both scales, ratio 300; undeclared it fails with the hint, declared it passes at 1:50 and with the same thickness at 1:500. A declared lump 2 x 3 x 3 mm: ratio 1.5, no sheet. A declared strip 300 x 10 x 1 mm: ratio 10, no sheet. A declared ribbon 300 x 1 x 0.04 mm: ratio 25, but 1 mm across is below the limit, no sheet. The garment layer of the sample figure declares 3 mm cotton on the torso: a 300 x 300 x 3 mm cotton plate bound to it passes without a flag; 1 mm thick it is off its gauge and fails without the hint, and declared it fails the declaration as well. A plate with `sheet` and `slender` fails for declaring both (`slender` exempts it from the thickness). A declared board 300 x 300 x 10 mm is thicker than 7.5 mm and 30 times as broad: the flag is in order. A declared block 300 x 300 x 20 mm: ratio 15, no sheet although nothing is below the limit. The two rib hoops (10 x 10 mm section, 212 and 178 mm across) at 1:500: both are 10 mm thin without the hint, because a hoop is a bent rod and no sheet; declared a sheet the hoop fails the declaration too (band 10 mm over thickness 10 mm: ratio 1). Declared `slender` both pass (`longMembers`).

sheets.hand: limit 7.5 mm (1:50), ratio 20. A feather vane as a loft 120 mm long with a lens section 24 x 1 mm: thickness 1, middle extent 24 >= max(7.5, 20 x 1 = 20): a sheet. The same vane 6 mm wide: 6 < 20, a strip, not a sheet (and not slender either: 120 / 6 = 20 would need the declaration). A lump 2 x 3 x 3 mm: 3 < 7.5, no sheet. A board 5 x 90 x 300 mm as a box: 90 < 20 x 5 = 100: no sheet; 4 mm thick: 90 >= 80: a sheet. A disc of 1 mm and 60 mm diameter as an ellipsoid: a sheet. With a declared gauge of 0.5 mm a 1 mm sheet is not at its gauge: no sheet. A ring is as broad as its band, not as its diameter: two rib hoops of the labrador (revolves of a closed 10 x 10 mm loop at radii of 96 and 79 mm, overall 10 x 212 x 239 and 10 x 178 x 187 mm) have a band of 10 mm, under the limit (7.5 mm here, and 10 < 20 x 10): neither is a sheet, although the diameter of the first is over 20 times its thickness and that of the second is not (by their diameters the two equal hoops were judged differently). A washer 1 mm thick from radius 5 to 50 mm has a band of 45 >= max(7.5, 20): a sheet.

raster.hand: The rule raster has a cell of a quarter feature, but at least 256 cells along the long side of what is compared and never a cell below 0.05 mm: a valve of 60 mm at 1:50 gets 0.06 / 256 = 0.234375 mm instead of 1.875 mm; a figure of 2 m keeps 1.875 mm; a table of 1.2 m at 1:500 gets 1.2 / 256 = 4.6875 mm instead of 18.75 mm; a part of 5 mm gets the floor. Two rectangles: A from (0.4, 0.3) to (60.7, 30.1) mm and B, the same 3 mm shorter at its right end: the intersection is B, the union is A, IoU = 57.3 / 60.3 = 0.950249. On cells of 1.875 mm the columns along the two right edges are in doubt, one column is 1.875 / 60.3 = 3.1 % of the union; on cells of 0.234375 mm one column is 0.39 %.

longMembers.hand: 1:500, feature 75 mm, a structure member counts as a bar from 2 x 75 = 150 mm of length and 5 times its largest cross extent (the forearm bones that `🧪️tests/🧊️model-skeleton` pins at their true shaft at every scale are 220 to 280 mm long). A femur as a loft 390 mm long with shaft radii of 14 to 17.5 mm: largest cross extent 35 mm, 390 / 35 = 11.1 >= 5 and 390 >= 150: declared `slender` it keeps its true section (no `volumes-feature`, no `volumes-slender` finding); not declared, its 28 mm shaft is below 75 mm and `volumes-feature` reports it. A radius as a loft 240 mm long with shaft radii of 7 to 9 mm: 240 / 18 = 13.3 >= 5 and 240 >= 150, declared `slender` it keeps its true section as well. A finger bone of 80 x 18 mm declared slender: 80 < 150, so it needs the general ratio 20 and has 4.4: `volumes-slender` reports it. The same femur in the body list is no structure member: 11.1 < 20, `volumes-slender` reports it. Two rib hoops with the same 10 x 10 mm section, 212 and 178 mm across: a hoop is slender by the centre line it follows (about 640 and 540 mm of circumference over 10 mm), so both pass once declared `slender`, in any list, and both are reported by `volumes-feature` when not declared: equal hoops, equal verdicts.

spans.hand: A `member` solid of the structure list may name in `members` the further bones it spans besides `member`. The names are bones of the rig, distinct, and form with `member` one connected piece of the rig (each the parent or a child of another); only a `member` part spans (`volume-member`, reported under `volumes-structure-coverage`). In the default pose each named bone, sampled at 9 evenly spaced points from its joint to its tip, lies in the solid or within one smallest feature of the scale of its surface (`spanGapM:<solid>:<bone>`, limit 7.5 mm at 1:50, 75 mm at 1:500). The solid then counts as the member solid of every named bone and is judged for `slender` by its own extents. `segments` measure a rod 20 x 300 x 20 mm standing on the ground at the origin (x and z from -0.01 to 0.01, y from 0 to 0.3). `cases` patch the sample figure, whose pelvis (0.1 m), torso (0.45 m) and head (0.22 m) stand in one vertical line and whose thigh (0.45 m) and shank (0.43 m) hang in one line below the hip; its member solids are capsules along the bones with a radius of 75 mm at 1:500 and 40 mm at 1:50. `coverage`, `feature` and `slender` count the findings of `volumes-structure-coverage` (without its `outsideBodyM` findings: the foot members of the sample figure reach beyond its body whatever the patch), `volumes-feature` and `volumes-slender`; `gaps` are the measured `spanGapM` values, compared within `gapToleranceM` because a capsule is a faceted mesh.
